title: Reduce lore-cli's GitHub Actions spend: platform matrices on tags/releases only, no nightly (OPAG-166)
description:
BRIEFED 2026-09-17 by opum-agent, not yet started. User ruling: the fleet's GitHub Actions bill exceeds all hosting and subscriptions combined, filed fleet-wide as opum-agent OPAG-166 (High).

lore-cli's share, as measured by opum-agent: $92.80 of a $280.07 17-day fleet total (the single largest repo cost), 47% of that macOS/Windows minutes, with CI running ~13 jobs per run across 242 PR runs this month.

DIRECTION, per the user ruling relayed: platform (native six-host) matrices should run on tags and releases only, not on every PR/push. This repo's release.yml already runs its six-host matrix only on workflow_dispatch against a tag (see CLAUDE.md's repo profile) -- the cost is concentrated in ci.yml's per-PR/per-push jobs (lint/typecheck/test on ubuntu+windows, docker e2e harness, browser qualification, scaffold smokes, etc.), which is the likely target, not release.yml.

TWO PITFALLS NAMED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR, from lessons already paid for elsewhere in the fleet -- read before touching ci.yml:

1. Do NOT add `cancel-in-progress` blanket-fashion to a concurrency group. quest-cli found a concurrency group that contained a job whose runs must not be cancelled -- a required check that also runs on the promotion path -- so cancelling mid-run made main's required checks unsatisfiable. Check what else shares a group before adding cancellation to it; a group is not the same as one workflow file.

2. Do NOT path-filter a workflow that carries required status checks. This is LCLI-196, already lived through in THIS repo: a path-filtered required check produces no run at all on a PR that doesn't touch the filtered paths, and a required-but-absent context blocks the PR forever rather than passing it (CLAUDE.md's own repo profile: "a required status check that names a job which no longer runs blocks every promotion forever while measuring nothing"). The five contexts required on `dev` (docker e2e harness, lint/typecheck/test ubuntu+windows, Tracker integrity, lore check) cannot be path-filtered without first removing them from the ruleset or restructuring how they're satisfied.

The user has authorised a self-hosted macOS runner on mini2 plus Linux/Windows VMs as an alternative to GitHub-hosted minutes for the expensive jobs -- registration is the user's own action, not this task's to perform, but the workflow should be written to be able to target it once registered.

NOT STARTED. No branch, no design decision made yet on which ci.yml jobs to cut, gate, or move to self-hosted runners. This record exists so the priority survives a session recycle rather than depending on the orchestrator re-briefing a successor from scratch -- this session watched a cursor get silently lost earlier today (OPAG-163) and is deliberately not repeating that by leaving fleet-priority context only in a relay.
